title: When the Worn Spirit Wants Repose
description: When the Worn Spirit Wants Repose in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Edmeston wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 7 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Lord's Day”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When the worn spir-it wants re-pose, And sighs her God to seek, How sweet to hail th'e-ve-ning's close That ends the wea-ry week!

lines: When the worn spirit wants repose,
And sighs her God to seek,
How sweet to hail the evening's close
How sweet to hail the early dawn
Beams its new rays of light!
Blest day! thine hours too soon will cease
Breathe, Heavenly Spirit, source of peace,

licence: Public domain: James Edmeston died in 1867.
credits: Words by James Edmeston (1791–1867), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
